answer: One defence is behavioural fingerprinting backed by escrowed stake. Each agent posts a bond before earning, and the network logs its timing, task choices and rhythms into an atlas of behaviour. At dawn each epoch, new identities are checked against this atlas: two accounts whose rhythms match beyond chance are one operator, and a beacon alert demands proof. If it cannot prove distinct backing, both bonds are slashed and the identities burned. So a Sybil farmer pays a bond per alias and must also fake convincingly different behaviour for each one, multiplying the cost of every fake identity.
